Beta — captain-intel sources not yet wired; picks rank on seasonal presence + SST fit + reef proximity until captain heat scores populate.

home_port.notes: Perdido Key primary — Gulf access via Perdido Pass. Alabama Artificial Reef Zone within 30-45nm, DeSoto Canyon (The Nipple) within 55-65nm on calm days, Cobia Alley on Randy's doorstep every March-April.

zones.name: Perdido Pass
zones.notes: The primary Gulf access from Perdido Key + Orange Beach. Deep pass with strong tide, great for redfish + trout on the jetties, cobia sight-fishing on the beach in spring, Spanish mackerel schools passing through summer.

zones.name: Perdido Bay
zones.notes: Back-bay behind Perdido Key. Excellent redfish + trout, especially in the fall pattern. Wade-fishing grass flats + oyster bars. Protected water when Gulf blows.

zones.name: Big Lagoon
zones.notes: Long back-bay E of Perdido Key. Grass flats + docks + drop-offs. Consistent trout year-round; redfish schools in the fall.

zones.name: The Massachusetts Wreck
zones.notes: WWI-era battleship wreck ~10nm SW of Pensacola Pass. Popular structure — amberjack, vermilion, kings + cobia in season. Well within Randy's day range.

zones.name: Alabama Artificial Reef Zone
zones.notes: World's largest artificial reef system — hundreds of numbers ~25-45 nm off Perdido Key/Gulf Shores. Snapper + grouper + amberjack. Randy's most productive bottom-fishing option.

zones.name: Trysler Grounds
zones.notes: Popular Alabama-side bottom-fishing area, ~40nm off Perdido. Public numbers get pressured but produce.

zones.name: The Timberholes
zones.notes: Sunken-timber bottom structure ~50nm SW of Pensacola Pass. Classic snapper/grouper. Deeper water, big fish.

zones.name: Pensacola Pass
zones.notes: Main Pensacola Bay inlet. Deep pass with jetty structure. Cobia migration sight-fishing in Mar-Apr. Kings + Spanish in warmer months.

zones.name: Pensacola Bay
zones.notes: Large back-bay system — Escambia + East Bay + Bayou Chico. Bull redfish schools + trout on flats. Bridges + rockpiles for structure.

zones.name: The Antares Wreck
zones.notes: Well-known wreck ~15nm S of Pensacola Pass. Amberjack + snapper + summer kings.

zones.name: Escambia County Public Reefs
zones.notes: Dozens of public artificial-reef numbers 5-25 nm S of Pensacola/Perdido. Snapper + grouper + kings. Great for family/short trips.

zones.name: The Nipple
zones.notes: The iconic DeSoto Canyon-edge spot — bottom drops from 200 to 1000+ ft. ~55-65nm SW of Pensacola Pass, within Randy's day range on calm days. Yellowfin, blackfin, marlin, mahi. Every Gulf offshore captain knows the Nipple.

zones.name: The Elbow
zones.notes: Deeper cousin of the Nipple, 10-15nm further SE. 1000-1500 ft. Big tuna + marlin. Edge of Randy's practical range on flat days.

zones.name: The Spur
zones.notes: North of the Nipple, ~40-50nm SW of Perdido Pass. Shallower ridge that concentrates bait. Yellowfin passing through, blackfin in numbers.

zones.name: DeSoto Canyon Head
zones.notes: Head of the DeSoto Canyon axis, ~70nm SW of Pensacola Pass. Deep-water marlin fishing when calm.

zones.name: Perdido Cobia Alley
zones.notes: 1-2nm off Perdido Key beach — the annual March-April cobia sight-fishing lane. Migration runs east-to-west along the beach. Best hours 10am-2pm with sun overhead.

zones.name: Pensacola Beach Cobia Alley
zones.notes: Continuation of the Cobia Alley off Pensacola Beach + Casino Beach. Same March-April pattern. Sight-fishing from towers.

zones.name: Navarre Beach Cobia Alley
zones.notes: Navarre Beach section of the spring cobia lane. Less pressure than Pensacola. Same water clarity + sight-fishing setup.

zones.name: East Pass (Destin Inlet)
zones.notes: Destin's Gulf access — deep pass, strong tide. Kings inside the pass in summer. Cobia in spring. Trout on the flats. 'World's Luckiest Fishing Village' launches from here.

zones.name: Choctawhatchee Bay
zones.notes: Big back-bay system behind Destin/Fort Walton. Grass flats + oyster bars + bridge structure. Consistent redfish + trout.

zones.name: The Edge (Destin)
zones.notes: The 100-fathom line ~15-25nm S of East Pass — where Destin's charter fleet lives. Steep bottom drop, permanent bait pile, tuna + kings + bottom action. Randy's best 'go anytime' Destin spot.

zones.name: The Steps
zones.notes: Terraced bottom structure past the Edge, ~25nm S of Destin. Amberjack magnet. Deeper water = bigger tuna when they show.

zones.name: Empire Mica Wreck
zones.notes: WWII British tanker torpedoed 1942 — 465ft long, 100ft depth, ~50nm SE of Destin. Legendary wreck. Amberjack + big grouper + kings above.

zones.name: Panama City Pass
zones.notes: PCB's Gulf access. Deep pass, tanker channel. Kings inside pass in summer + cobia on the beach nearby in spring.

zones.name: St. Andrews Bay
zones.notes: PCB back-bay + North Bay + West Bay complex. Grass flats, drop-offs, dock lights. Classic redfish + trout year-round.

zones.name: Bay County Public Reefs
zones.notes: Dozens of public artificial reef numbers 5-25 nm S of PCB. Snapper + grouper + kings. Bay County Artificial Reef Association maintains an active list.

zones.name: Warsaw Reef
zones.notes: Prominent artificial reef ~30nm SW of PCB. Big amberjack + grouper. Deeper water than the public inshore reefs.

zones.name: Sherman Wreck
zones.notes: WWII Liberty ship wreck sunk as reef ~28nm S of PCB. 441ft long, 90ft depth. Reliable amberjack + grouper spot.

zones.name: Grouper Alley
zones.notes: The 100ft depth line ~30nm SE of PCB — Gag + red grouper on live structure. Named for the concentration of grouper hard bottom.

zones.name: PCB Beach Cobia Alley
zones.notes: PCB beach section of the spring cobia migration. Later than Perdido/Pensacola — cobia often peak here late Mar/early Apr. Sight-fish from tower.

zones.name: Cape San Blas
zones.notes: The hook of Cape San Blas concentrates bait. Cobia stage here in migration. Tarpon show in summer. King mackerel schools work the beach.

zones.name: Apalachicola Bay
zones.notes: Big-water back-bay behind St. George Island. Famous oyster grounds (historically). Trophy trout + redfish, summer tarpon in the passes (Bob Sikes Cut, West Pass).

zones.name: St. George Island
zones.notes: 14-mi barrier island east of Apalachicola. Beach + surf fishing, tarpon on the outside in summer, cobia migration late March. Bob Sikes Cut is the local pass.

zones.name: USS Oriskany
zones.notes: WORLD'S LARGEST ARTIFICIAL REEF — 911ft aircraft carrier sunk 2006 as reef, ~24nm SE of Pensacola Pass. Top of superstructure at ~85ft, deck at ~140ft, bottom 212ft. Legendary amberjack + snapper + grouper. Every Pensacola charter runs here. Randy's within range on flat days.

zones.name: YDT-14 & YDT-15 Wrecks
zones.notes: Two Navy dive-tender wrecks sunk as reef ~5-8nm SW of Pensacola Pass, 90ft depth. Popular with charter fleet — snapper, grouper, amberjack. Very close to home port.

zones.name: Pete Tide II Wreck
zones.notes: Sunken tug wreck ~8nm SW of Pensacola Pass, 100ft. Consistent snapper + amberjack producer.

zones.name: Chevron Reef
zones.notes: Decommissioned Chevron oil rig sunk as artificial reef ~15nm S of Destin. Structure attracts amberjack + snapper + kings. Also called 'The Chevron.'

zones.name: Chickenbone Wreck
zones.notes: Barge wreck ~8nm SE of East Pass Destin. Local favorite for shorter charter trips. Snapper + grouper + kings.

zones.name: SS United States Artificial Reef
zones.notes: America's greatest ocean liner (990ft) deployed as artificial reef ~24nm SW of Destin East Pass in 2025-26. Poised to be the largest wreck-reef in the Gulf after Oriskany. Massive superstructure = massive bait pile = pelagic + bottom action. Bucket-list destination.

zones.name: The Grey Ghost Wreck
zones.notes: WWII-era tug ~9nm SW of Panama City Pass, 90ft depth. Part of the Florida Panhandle Shipwreck Trail. Reliable snapper + grouper + amberjack.

zones.name: USS Accokeek
zones.notes: Navy sub-chaser wreck ~14nm S of PCB, 100ft. Historic wreck on the Panhandle Shipwreck Trail. Big amberjack, snapper.

zones.name: Vamar Wreck
zones.notes: WWII British freighter wreck ~4nm off Mexico Beach, 75ft depth. Sank 1942. Well-scattered debris field concentrates bait. Grouper + snapper + kings.

zones.name: SS Tarpon
zones.notes: Historic 1937 steamship wreck ~10nm SW of PCB Pass, 95ft. One of the Panhandle Shipwreck Trail's originals. Amberjack + snapper concentration.

zones.name: USS Strength
zones.notes: WWII minesweeper wreck ~7nm off Mexico Beach, 75ft. Part of the Panhandle Shipwreck Trail. Big amberjack, red snapper in season.

zones.name: Hathaway Bridge Rubble
zones.notes: Old Hathaway Bridge sections deployed as artificial reef ~3-5nm off PCB. Multiple pile-driven concrete piers concentrate bait. Snapper + grouper + kings + Spanish.

zones.name: Pensacola Beach Pier
zones.notes: 1,471ft-long pier off Pensacola Beach — jack crevalle, kings, Spanish mackerel, cobia sight-fishing in spring, flounder around pilings. Fish from the pier OR anchor a boat 100 yds off.

zones.name: Russell-Fields (PCB) Pier
zones.notes: 1,500ft PCB pier off Pier Park. Kings + Spanish + cobia + trout. Pier pilings + bait attracts pelagics. Boat anchors just off the end also produce.

zones.name: Nick Reef (AL)
zones.notes: Popular named Alabama Public Reef ~35nm S of Perdido Pass, mixed structure (barges + junk cars). Reliable snapper + grouper.

zones.name: Bill's Barge (AL)
zones.notes: Sunken barge in Alabama Public Reef Zone ~40nm S of Perdido Pass. Big amberjack, red snapper. Public number gets pressured.

zones.name: Fort Morgan Rig Cluster
zones.notes: Cluster of shallow-water Alabama state rigs 15-25nm SW of Perdido Pass, 60-150ft depth. Amberjack + snapper + kings + spring cobia. Randy's most reachable rig cluster.

zones.name: Dauphin Island Rig Cluster
zones.notes: Shallow Alabama rigs near Mobile Bay entrance, 30-40nm W of Perdido Pass. Big amberjack + snapper. Similar productivity to Fort Morgan cluster.

zones.name: Mobile Bay Ship Channel Rigs
zones.notes: Rigs bordering the Mobile Bay ship channel 25-30nm W of Perdido Pass. Kings + Spanish + cobia + snapper.

zones.name: Petronius Platform
zones.notes: 1754ft-tall compliant tower — one of world's tallest freestanding structures — 100nm SSW of Perdido Pass. Iconic deepwater tuna + marlin destination. OUT OF RANGE for Randy's 28' Cobia from Perdido; reachable from Louisiana/MS ports or larger boat. Legendary yellowfin, wahoo, blue marlin.

zones.name: Ram Powell TLP
zones.notes: Tension-leg oil platform in 3200ft water — 105nm SSW of Perdido Pass. Yellowfin + marlin bucket-list destination. OUT OF RANGE from Perdido — reachable via LA/MS or larger boat. Massive structure = massive bait aggregation.

zones.name: Marlin TLP
zones.notes: Tension-leg platform 95nm SSW of Perdido Pass. Yellowfin + blue marlin. Near-OOR from Perdido, more accessible from LA.

zones.name: Devil's Tower Spar
zones.notes: Deepwater Dominion Energy spar platform 160nm SSW of Perdido — 5610ft water. Bigeye + yellowfin + blue marlin. Louisiana Venice / Grand Isle destination. Included for LA-based visitors + larger-boat charters.

zones.name: Midnight Lump (Sackett Bank)
zones.notes: Legendary sea-mount 15nm SW of Mississippi River mouth — winter yellowfin destination for LA. Salt dome rises from 400ft to 200ft. OUT OF RANGE from Perdido; Venice LA is the launch port. Included so a LA-based visitor picking Venice as home port instantly gets it.

zones.name: Callon Jacket
zones.notes: Decommissioned oil rig jacket sunk as artificial reef ~70nm SSW of Perdido Pass. Big amberjack, wandering yellowfin/blackfin, kings. Deepwater edge for Randy — flat-calm days only. State-published (AL Marine Resources).

zones.name: Marathon Jacket
zones.notes: Sunken Marathon Oil rig jacket ~55nm SSW of Perdido Pass. Reachable for Randy on calm days. Amberjack + snapper + passing yellowfin. State-published (AL Marine Resources).

zones.name: Unocal Rig
zones.notes: Deepwater Unocal rig jacket ~75nm SSW of Perdido — big tuna + blue marlin habitat. Edge of Randy's range in flat conditions. State-published (AL Marine Resources).

zones.name: M/V LuLu
zones.notes: 271ft coastal freighter sunk 2013 as artificial reef ~17nm S of Perdido Pass. Now a classic AL dive-fish site. Amberjack + snapper + grouper. Fully within Randy's day range. State-published (AL Marine Resources).

zones.name: Lipscomb Tug
zones.notes: Sunken tug ~20nm SW of Perdido Pass. Reliable snapper/amberjack producer, part of the Fort Morgan-area reef complex. State-published (AL Marine Resources).

zones.name: 105 Tug
zones.notes: Sunken 105ft tug ~15nm SSW of Perdido Pass. Snapper/amberjack on classic AL nearshore reef. State-published (AL Marine Resources).

zones.name: Enhanced Wreck #1
zones.notes: AL Marine Resources 'Enhanced Wreck' program — vessel supplemented with reef modules ~17nm SSW of Perdido Pass. Snapper + grouper + amberjack. State-published.

zones.name: Nail Ship
zones.notes: Sunken ship reef ~35nm W of Perdido Pass, off Mobile Bay. Big amberjack + snapper. State-published (AL Marine Resources).

zones.name: Three Mile Barge
zones.notes: Iconic AL barge reef ~3nm S of Perdido Beach — closest big-structure spot to Randy's home port. Snapper + kings + Spanish. State-published (AL Marine Resources).

zones.name: Rookie Barge
zones.notes: Sunken barge ~10nm SSW of Perdido Pass. Reliable snapper spot in AL public reef zone. State-published.

zones.name: Buffalo Barge
zones.notes: Sunken 'Buffalo' barge ~17nm SW of Perdido Pass. Part of the extensive AL barge reef complex. State-published.

zones.name: Perdido Weir
zones.notes: Underwater weir/breakwater structure ~10nm S of Perdido Pass. Named AL Marine Resources reef. Cobia sight-fishing lane passes through in spring.

zones.name: Poseidon Playground
zones.notes: Ecological reef complex ~2nm S of Perdido Beach — pyramids/modules designed for juvenile snapper habitat. Named AL Marine Resources site.

zones.name: Pat Jones Pyramids
zones.notes: Concrete pyramid reef modules ~3nm SW of Perdido Pass. Snapper aggregation site. State-published (AL Marine Resources).

zones.name: Atlantic Drydock (D.R. Dunlap)
zones.notes: Sunken drydock ~28nm SW of Perdido Pass. Massive steel structure, big amberjack + grouper. State-published (AL Marine Resources).

zones.name: Gulf State Park Reef Complex
zones.notes: State Park reef complex 0.5-2nm off Romar Beach + Alabama Point + Gulf State Park Pier. Three named modules. Sight-fishing + snapper + kings. Great family/short-trip spot from Perdido.

zones.name: Bay Marchand 3
zones.notes: Bay Marchand oil-field artificial reef — Louisiana rigs-to-reefs deployment. Yellowfin passes through, snapper/amberjack on the jacket. OUT OF RANGE from Perdido; Venice LA is the launch port. State-published (LA Wildlife & Fisheries).

zones.name: Cat Island Reef Complex
zones.notes: MS Marine Resources reef complex near Cat Island — barrier island south of Gulfport. 30+ deployed reef modules. Inshore/nearshore trout + reds + flounder. State-published.

zones.name: Mexico Rock
zones.notes: Natural hard-bottom limestone rock ~7nm S of Perdido Pass — one of the closest natural structures. Snapper + grouper year-round. Popular short-run spot for Randy's home port.

zones.name: Whitney Bank
zones.notes: Natural bank feature adjacent to Mexico Rock, ~7nm S of Perdido Pass. Snapper + grouper. Companion spot to Mexico Rock on same run.

zones.name: Perdido Pass Bridge Complex
zones.notes: Seven old Perdido Pass Bridge sections sunk as reef 12-14nm S of Perdido Pass. Solid concrete structure holds snapper, kings, spring cobia. Named AL Marine Resources sites (Bridges 1-7).

zones.name: CSX Boxcars
zones.notes: Sunken CSX railroad boxcars ~17nm S of Perdido Pass. Unique steel structure = strong snapper + grouper aggregation. State-published (AL Marine Resources).

zones.name: Randy Hopper Reef
zones.notes: Named memorial reef ~14nm SW of Perdido Pass. Snapper + kings. State-published.

zones.name: Harris Memorial Reef
zones.notes: Named memorial reef ~13.5nm SW of Perdido Pass. Snapper + amberjack. State-published (AL Marine Resources).

zones.name: Captain Shirley Brown
zones.notes: Named vessel/memorial reef ~13nm S of Perdido Pass. Snapper concentration. State-published.

zones.name: USCG Anchors
zones.notes: Field of scattered Coast Guard anchors sunk as reef ~19nm SW of Perdido Pass. Unique low-relief structure. Snapper + kings + cobia. State-published.

zones.name: New Venture
zones.notes: Sunken 'New Venture' vessel ~22nm S of Perdido Pass. Big amberjack + grouper. State-published (AL Marine Resources).

zones.name: Hunt Reef
zones.notes: Named reef ~21nm SW of Perdido Pass. Snapper + grouper on classic mid-shelf structure. State-published.

zones.name: Southeast Banks
zones.notes: Natural mid-shelf bank feature ~25nm SW of Perdido Pass. High-relief bottom = big snapper + grouper. State-recognized natural fishing area.

zones.name: Papa Joe (John Wood) Reef
zones.notes: Memorial reef in the Mobile Bay approaches ~34nm W of Perdido Pass. Named AL Marine Resources site — snapper + amberjack.

zones.name: Lundstrom Reefs (William + Elizabeth + Lainey)
zones.notes: Cluster of 3 named memorial reefs (William Lundstrom, Elizabeth Lundstrom, Lainey) ~39nm SW of Perdido Pass. Snapper + grouper. State-published.

zones.name: Marathon Reef
zones.notes: Named reef ~49nm SSW of Perdido Pass — deep-water bottom fishing. Big red snapper. State-published (AL Marine Resources). Different from Marathon Jacket.

zones.name: Swingle Reef
zones.notes: Deep-water named reef ~52nm SSW of Perdido Pass. Edge of Randy's practical range but reachable on calm days. Snapper + grouper. State-published.

zones.name: Timber Holes (ES-2 FL)
zones.notes: FL Panhandle prehistoric-forest limestone ledges — one of the region's most unique natural bottom features. FL Escambia County site ES-2 (Florida FWC). Big grouper + snapper. Coords approximate; verify from FL FWC coordinate list.

zones.name: Brass Wreck (ES-5 FL)
zones.notes: 250-ft wooden-hull schooner wreck from the late 1800s (aka Anchor Wreck). FL Escambia County site ES-5 (Florida FWC). Historic wreck, snapper + amberjack. Coords approximate.

zones.name: Tenneco Platform (ES-10 FL)
zones.notes: 130x80x90 ft oil rig platform (2 jacket pieces side by side) sunk as artificial reef off Escambia County. FL FWC site ES-10. Big amberjack + snapper. Coords verified from FL FWC ES0004 (Aug 2026).

zones.name: The Nipple East (ES-7 FL)
zones.notes: Blue-water trolling area east of the main Nipple — FL FWC site ES-7. Yellowfin, marlin, mahi. Companion spot to The Nipple + The Elbow. Coords approximate.

zones.name: Chevron Platform (FL ES0053)
zones.notes: Chevron oil rig platform sunk as artificial reef ~4nm S of Pensacola Beach. NOT the Destin Chevron Reef — separate spot. Real coords from FL FWC. Kings + amberjack + snapper. Very close to Pensacola Pass.

zones.name: Joe Patti Memorial Reef
zones.notes: Memorial reef named for the famous Pensacola seafood market founder. ~17nm S of Pensacola Pass. FL FWC ES0189 — coords verified. Snapper + grouper + amberjack.

zones.name: Tug Ocean Wind
zones.notes: Sunken tug boat wreck ~7nm SW of Pensacola Pass. FL FWC ES0048 — coords verified. Snapper + amberjack + kings on intact hull.

zones.name: I-10 Bridge Reef Cluster
zones.notes: Old Interstate 10 bridge sections sunk as 7 separate reef sites 10-12nm S of Perdido Pass. FL FWC ES0122-ES0128 — verified. Snapper + kings + spring cobia.

zones.name: CSX Rubble Site (FL)
zones.notes: Sunken CSX railroad rubble ~14nm S of Pensacola Pass. FL FWC ES0010 — verified. Steel + concrete debris = strong snapper habitat. Different from AL CSX Boxcars.

zones.name: Concrete Pyramids Cluster (FL)
zones.notes: Cluster of concrete pyramid reef modules ~13nm S of Pensacola Pass. FL FWC ES0056-ES0059 — verified. Snapper + kings + Spanish.

zones.name: Pensacola Bay Fishing Bridge Reef
zones.notes: Old Pensacola Bay fishing bridge sections sunk as reef ~12nm S of Perdido Pass. FL FWC ES0107 — verified.

zones.name: Soule Concrete Modules Cluster
zones.notes: Multiple Soule concrete reef modules ~13nm S of Pensacola. FL FWC ES0044-ES0047 — verified. Prefabricated snapper habitat.

zones.name: Blackwater Bridge I-10 Reef
zones.notes: Old Blackwater Bridge (I-10 crossing) sections sunk as reef ~14nm S of Pensacola Pass. FL FWC ES0076-ES0078 — verified.
